why: The policy describes how requirements are derived, but the security requirements list itself is not in the evidence.
Policy 4.0 approved by management on 14 July 2026 and signed by both managing directors.
The policy states its objectives and why security matters to the business.
Intranet export shows all policies published and viewed by 163 of 171 employees.
Change notices were sent to employees and to suppliers via the supplier portal.
Requirements come from the business plan, customer contracts and German law.
No document states consequences for non-conformance.
Nine supporting standards and procedures exist and are published.
Review cycles are defined, and the yearly policy review was done on 1 July 2026.
Reportable events cover personnel, physical, IT and supplier cases, and are taught in the training most staff completed.
Email, ticket and hotline channels are defined and were used for 43 reports.
The security desk gives reporters feedback, and the register records it.
The security desk is the single point of contact.
A hotline for urgent events sits alongside email and tickets, and both were used.
The duty to report is in the employment contract and is covered in the yearly training.
A supplier's report was handled promptly, but no channel for external parties is defined or communicated.
Contact details are on the intranet start page and on posters by every time clock.
Feedback within two working days is defined and recorded for every report.
Every report was recorded within one working day, with a median of 3 hours to first action.
Register entries show fitting actions taken and closed.
Reviews after incidents are defined, but none is recorded for incidents 2026-007 and 2026-031.
Reports are categorized, qualified and prioritized in the register.
Owners by category, coordination, urgent channels and deputies are defined; qualification and resources are not.
No strategy for reporting criminal aspects to authorities.
97 percent completed the basic course, and target-group sessions were held.
The concept covers most topics, but not compliance issues of information security.
Administrators, managers, customer-network and prototype staff get their own training.
Management approved the concept on 16 February 2026.
The course runs yearly, and a briefing went out after phishing incident 2026-007.
The e-learning platform records completions, and session attendance is listed.
The information security officer and security desk are named in courses, on the intranet and on posters.
Sign-in methods are chosen by exposure, with a second factor for internet-facing systems.
12-character minimum, breached-password blocking and national authority guidance are applied.
Sign-in procedures are defined and shown configured in the rollout record.
Directory settings enforce strong passwords.
All 9 administrator accounts require hardware security keys.
Joiner, mover and leaver tickets show accounts created, changed and deleted.
Named personal accounts; the review confirmed every account belongs to a current employee.
Shared accounts are limited to read-only production display terminals, each registered.
Every leaver account was disabled by the end of the last working day.
Six-monthly reviews were done in January and in mid-2026.
Secure handover is defined, but there is no record of it being done.
All login-information aspects are defined, and password quality is enforced in the directory.
A standard employee role with minimal rights is used for new accounts.
Nothing addresses manufacturer default accounts or passwords.
Accounts are requested by managers and approved by system owners.
A second person, the system owner, approved every joiner account.
End dates are defined, but the review found three finished supplier accounts still active.
Disable on the last working day, delete after 90 days.
No technical prevention of default passwords is shown.
Authenticator apps and hardware keys are used, but no rules for securing the medium are given.
Regular reviews happen, but accounts in customers' systems were excluded.
Nothing prevents interactive login for technical accounts.
Request, approval, least privilege and revocation are defined and shown in tickets and the review.
Six-monthly reviews cover all account types, but not access in customers' systems.
The policy sets a job-based, start-from-no-access strategy.
Rights are bundled into owned roles, and 14 roles were reviewed.
Rights are granted by role and job need.
Admin rights are held only by separate administrator accounts.
Mover tickets remove old roles, but the review found 11 rights left over from role changes.
Strong algorithms are set out, but the encryption standard (approved 2022, yearly cycle) is stale.
The concept covers methods, key strengths and key lifecycle, but the standard is past its review cycle.
Network services and approved outside services are registered.
Rules by classification are defined and reflected in the register.
TLS was enforced and verified by an external scan on 8 September 2026.
No measures for correct addressing or delivery are described.
Transport and end-to-end encryption are applied by classification.
Logging requirements are defined, and logs are collected and reviewed.
Administrator and user sign-ins and changes are logged under named accounts.
A logging scope list assesses each system's need, checked on 9 March 2026.
The providers' monitoring options are known but were not considered when approving them.
Monthly log reviews are recorded with their findings.
Findings were escalated to the security desk as events.
The central log server is said to be protected, but no record shows it.
No network-level monitoring is described.
Advisories are gathered nightly from manufacturers and the CVE database, and scored with CVSS.
Affected assets and priorities are recorded per CVE.
Each vulnerability is patched, scheduled or risk-accepted.
Patching is tracked, but no defined patch process or testing is shown, and one item is overdue.
RA-2026-03 limits the CAD vault to the design VLAN and logs downloads.
No check that installed patches succeeded is shown.
No backup concept in the evidence.
No recovery concept in the evidence.
No backup and recovery concept per IT service.
